Part 2&3 地点 PLACE

Describe an interesting building

描述一座有趣的建筑

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe an interesting building

  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • What it looks like (它看起来什么样)
  • What function it has (它有什么功能)
  • And explain why you think it is interesting (并解释为什么你觉得它有趣)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe an interesting building

OK, I'd like to talk about the Shenzhen Bay Sports Centre, which people here call the "Spring Cocoon". It's in the Nanshan district of my city, right next to Shenzhen Bay Park, so it's quite close to the sea. As for what it looks like, that's actually the most striking thing about it. The building has a huge oval shape, and the roof is made of white steel frames that curve and cross each other, like a giant silkworm cocoon, which is exactly where the nickname comes from. Inside there's a big open courtyard, and the whole structure is surrounded by glass, so it looks really bright and modern, especially at night when the lights come on. The main function of the building is as a sports and event venue. It was built for the World University Games back in 2011, and these days it's used for all sorts of things, like swimming competitions, concerts and public sports. People can go there to play basketball or use the gym, and I've actually been there a couple of times to watch events. I think the reason it's so interesting to me is that it looks nothing like the normal box-shaped buildings around it. I mean, it really stands out as a landmark, and it's a great example of how a modern city can use creative architecture. Every time I pass by, it catches my eye, and I feel a little proud that my city has such a distinctive building.

讲的是深圳湾体育中心（春茧），在南山区、紧邻深圳湾公园靠海；外形是白色钢架曲线交织的巨型椭圆，像蚕茧，夜晚灯光下很现代；主要作为体育和活动场馆，2011年大运会建，现在用于游泳比赛、演唱会和公众健身；之所以有趣是因为它和周围方盒子建筑完全不同，是城市地标，每次路过都让人骄傲。

Q2What types of buildings are popular in your country?

Well, I'd say modern high-rise buildings are the most popular in my country at the moment, especially in big cities. Most new residential areas are made up of tall apartment blocks, because land is expensive and cities are crowded. At the same time, there's also a growing interest in traditional architecture, I think, since a lot of people enjoy visiting ancient temples and old streets. So it really depends on where you are, to be honest.

目前国内最流行的是现代高层建筑，尤其大城市，住宅多为高层公寓楼，因为地贵人多；同时也有对传统建筑的兴趣，很多人爱逛古寺老街；所以因地区而异。

Q3Is it worth spending a lot of money on the exterior appearance of a building?

I think it's worth it up to a point. On the one hand, a nice exterior can make a city more attractive and give people a sense of pride, and famous landmarks often become the symbol of a city. On the other hand, spending too much on the appearance while ignoring the inside could be a waste, because the people using the building care more about comfort and function. So I'd say there should be a balance between the two.

在一定程度上值得：好看的外立面让城市更有吸引力、带来自豪感，地标还成为城市象征；但过度注重外表而忽略内部是浪费，使用者更在乎舒适和功能；所以应两者平衡。

Q4Is it more important for a building to look good on the outside or on the inside?

To be honest, I think the inside matters more in daily life, because that's where people spend their time. A comfortable interior affects how well people work, study or rest, and nobody really wants to stay in a pretty building that's dark and uncomfortable. Having said that, the outside still matters in a way, since it's the first thing people see and it shapes the image of a neighbourhood. So both matter, but I'd say the inside probably comes first.

内部更重要，因为那是人们实际待的地方，舒适的室内影响工作学习和休息，没人想待在外表漂亮但阴暗不舒服的楼里；不过外部也有作用，它是第一印象、塑造街区形象；两者都重要但内部优先。

Q5Why do people like to visit historical sites?

I think there are a few reasons. First, historical sites let people connect with the past, I mean, they can imagine how people lived hundreds of years ago, which is a completely different experience from just reading about it in books. Second, these places are often beautiful and unique, so they make great spots for taking photos. Also, visiting them gives people a sense of cultural identity, especially in a country with such a long history.

有几个原因：历史遗址让人与过去相连，能想象几百年前人们怎么生活，和读书完全不同；这些地方通常美丽独特，适合拍照；还能带来文化认同感，尤其对有悠久历史的国家。

Q6待补充

I'd say yes, it's reasonable, but it should depend on the situation. If a building needs constant maintenance, then charging a fee makes sense, because repairs cost a lot of money and someone has to cover the cost. However, for public buildings, I think the fee should be kept low, or even free for students and elderly people, so that everyone can enjoy them. Otherwise, these places might only be for tourists who can afford it, which doesn't feel fair.

合理但要分情况：需要持续维护的建筑收费说得过去，维修很花钱；但对公共建筑应收费低些，对学生老人免费，让所有人都能参观，否则就只服务得起付得起的游客，不公平。

Q7Is it better to live in a new building or an old one?

Generally speaking, new buildings are more practical, I think, because they have better facilities, like lifts, good insulation and modern heating systems, and they're usually safer too. That said, old buildings have their own charm, such as thick walls and high ceilings, and some people really enjoy that traditional style. So for me personally, I'd choose a new building for daily comfort, but I can understand why others prefer the character of older ones.

通常新建筑更实用：设施更好，有电梯、好的隔热和供暖，也更安全；但老建筑有自己的魅力，比如厚墙高天花板，有人喜欢传统风格；个人会选新建筑图舒适，也理解别人偏爱老建筑的气质。
